WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoiced_order_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
), shares AS (
    SELECT gender, invoiced_order_count,
           1.0 * invoiced_order_count / SUM(invoiced_order_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_counts
), scored AS (
    SELECT gender, invoiced_order_count, share,
           share - AVG(share) OVER () AS above_average
    FROM shares
)
SELECT gender, invoiced_order_count, share, above_average
FROM scored
WHERE above_average > 0

assumptions.assumption: Counts each invoice as an invoiced order; if an order has multiple invoices, it contributes once per invoice. Customers without a linked invoice are excluded, and NULL gender is grouped as its own gender.
